svg.title: ToolForge on Azure — application architecture
svg.desc: A left-to-right, cut-paper architecture diagram based on the supplied ToolForge brief. Browser and external MCP clients reach public HTTPS ingress on Azure Container Apps. Every replica contains Next.js with Copilot, a localhost Python MCP server, and disposable local working storage in the same container. Published Python tools execute with host permissions. Azure App Service is an alternative host. Connected services are Microsoft Entra ID with separate web and MCP registrations, Azure OpenAI or Microsoft Foundry, Key Vault, optional Blob Storage, Azure Monitor, Container Registry, and PostgreSQL Flexible Server through a private endpoint and private DNS using compute VNet integration. Git and optional external MCP servers and downstream APIs are outside the application boundary. Dashed arrows denote optional integrations and container deployment. Two-headed arrows denote two-way exchanges. Small pins are routing joins, not extra services. This is an SVG companion to the editable Paperweave JSON, not a live-board screenshot.
svg.text: Collaborative Python tools, from browser and Copilot to published MCP execution. A logical architecture based on the supplied brief.

g.text: Compute VNet integration · private PostgreSQL connectivity
TOOLFORGE APPLICATION · Azure Container Apps (primary hosting)
tool execution · delegated auth where configured

svg.text: Published Python tools execute with the host's permissions.

g.text: Alternative hosting: Azure App Service · same container architecture, not an additional hop
Solid arrows = core paths. Dashed arrows = optional integration or container image deployment.
↔ = two-way exchanges. Small unlabelled pins are routing joins, not services.
Public HTTPS ingress remains public; compute VNet integration provides the private database path.
